newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-GRAF ITCHING TO GET HOME AFTER FATHER'S RELEASE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF ITCHING TO GET HOME AFTER FATHER'S RELEASE.

text.p: Steffi Graf said on Saturday that she had been unable to sleep through the last days of her father's 15 months in prison and was desperate to get back to Germany after his release on bail on Friday.

Speaking in Philadelphia where she is playing a tournament, Graf told reporters that she would continue with her playing commitments in the United States in the next nine days including next week's WTA Tour championship in New York, also known as the Masters.

But in an interview published in Germany, she said: "I wish this tournament and the Masters were already over. I can't wait to get back to Germany when the Masters is over. I talked with my father on the telephone on Friday."
Asked whether the last few days had been very emotional, Graf added: "Very emotional. I have hardly been able to sleep the last few nights but I hope that is all over now."

Peter Graf, who has acted as Steffi's full-time manager since she was eight years old, paid five million marks ($3.3 million) in bail and headed home from prison after being held in custody during a German court trial on tax evasion charges.
The Mannheim court has yet to decide whether 58-year-old Graf is guilty of the allegations of evading 19 million marks ($13 million) of tax on his daughter's earnings between 1989 and 1993.
Graf still has to report to police twice a week and receive pyschotherapy. His mental health during his time in custody has been the subject of German newspaper speculation.

But for the world's leading female player, who has always had a close relationship with her father, his release from prison has come as a big relief. She has broken down several times in public when asked about the scandal.
"I'm so happy for my father and my family," Graf said. "It is just a shame that I can't be in Germany today."

The release of former second-hand car salesman Graf was given front-page coverage in Germany's newspapers and a leading national television network changed its prime-time viewing schedule on Friday to run a special programme on the affair.

Graf's form dipped when the newspapers were full of stories of Peter's relationship with a topless model in 1990. But Graf has shown maturity beyond her 27 years during this scandal and produced some superb tennis during the last 15 months.

Asked how she has been able to keep up her form despite the emotion of the affair, Graf said: "I must admit, that is a puzzle to me sometimes. I'm playing good tennis here..It helps that I am fortunate enough to be playing without any injuries."
